claim.why_it_matters: A heading at the wrong level (or none) misplaces the clause in the outline that page_workunit, citation and section lookups read, so the clause is attributed to the wrong parent or not found as a section.
claim.note: Section heading printed in the PDF is transcribed as a plain paragraph with no Markdown heading marker, so it is lost from the document outline; should be '## 7.4 DATA DIVISION ENTRIES' (siblings such as 7.2.4 / 7.2 carry headings).

verdict.reasoning: The printed page IV-43 (PDF p189) shows '7.4 DATA DIVISION ENTRIES' as a numbered section heading in the same style as 7.3 and 7.2.5. In specs/ANSI_COBOL_1985.md (line 7872) it is a plain line with no '#' marker, whereas the same chapter's earlier siblings on pp187-188 are headings ('# 7. REFERENCE FORMAT', '## 7.1', '## 7.2 REFERENCE FORMAT REPRESENTATION', '### 7.2.1'..'### 7.2.4'). So 7.4 is missing from the outline; the correct form is '## 7.4 DATA DIVISION ENTRIES', matching '## 7.2'. The text itself is identical; the defect is purely the lost heading marker, as the claim says. (Same page also leaves 7.2.5, 7.3, 7.3.1-7.3.3 as plain lines; those are separate instances.)
